claims.statement: The cloud relay is the gateway's optional push-style outbound bridge with three responsibilities — device registration, 60s heartbeat, and incoming-SMS event upload — all implemented in com.autonomousone.messages.gateway (RegistrationManager, HeartbeatManager, WebhookEngine) and all funneling through the single BackendClient HTTP client; the components are supervised by ConnectionSupervisor alongside the LAN server and GMweb poller.

BackendClient performs JSON-only POST requests with 15s connect and 30s read timeouts, a User-Agent of AndroidGateway/<APP_VERSION>, and returns a sealed Result<T> (Success with body+status, or Failure with error, optional httpStatus, and isAuthError flag) so no exceptions leak to callers.

HTTPS is enforced at two layers for the cloud backend URL: GatewayPreferences.backendUrl's setter trims whitespace and trailing slash, allows empty (which clears the override), and requires https:// otherwise throwing IllegalArgumentException; and BackendClient.post re-checks prefs.backendUrl at request time and returns Failure("Insecure backend URL rejected — HTTPS required") without opening a connection, so the bearer token can never travel over plaintext HTTP.

The documented backend contract (docs/api/README.md and openapi.yaml x-cloud-backend-contract) has exactly three app-to-backend endpoints: POST /api/gateways/register (no bearer token, optional X-Registration-Secret) with body {deviceId, name, appVersion, androidVersion, deviceModel}; POST /api/gateways/heartbeat (Bearer) with body {appVersion, batteryLevel, networkType, timestamp}; POST /api/gateways/events/sms (Bearer) with body {eventId stable UUID, type sms.received, sender, message, timestamp} where eventId dedupes replays; all require HTTPS.

RegistrationManager.register() posts the device payload unauthenticated (authenticated=false so no bearer header is attached); deviceId is Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID (unique per app signing key, reset on factory reset) with a fallback to a random 32-hex ID generated once and persisted as deviceFallbackId when ANDROID_ID is blank or unreadable, and name/deviceModel are 'MANUFACTURER MODEL'.

The optional registrationSecret pairing secret (Keystore-encrypted, user-savable from the cloud card via saveRegistrationSecret) is sent as the X-Registration-Secret header on POST /api/gateways/register only when non-blank, so the backend can reject unauthenticated registration attempts that would hijack or invalidate the gateway; clearing it in the UI logs that the backend must then allow open registration.

Registration is idempotent on the backend side keyed by deviceId: ensureRegistered() short-circuits to true when isRegistered and the token are present, and on token loss a re-registration issues a new token that invalidates the old one; register() blocks without consent, and on a 2xx response parses gatewayId and token from the body, persists both (token encrypted) and sets isRegistered=true, while a failure or parse error returns false without touching stored credentials.

HeartbeatManager sends a heartbeat every 60s (HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000) with payload {appVersion, batteryLevel, networkType, timestamp}: batteryLevel is 0-100 percent or -1 on error, and networkType is 'mobile' when TelephonyManager data state is DATA_CONNECTED otherwise 'unknown' (Wi-Fi detection deliberately omitted as it would need an extra permission).

On heartbeat failure the manager sets state DISCONNECTED and sleeps an exponential backoff doubling from INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS 1s to a MAX_BACKOFF_MS 5-minute cap; success resets backoffMs to 1s, sets CONNECTED, and waits the 60s interval; both waits run as withTimeoutOrNull over a conflated wake Channel so they are interruptible.

BackendClient classifies HTTP 401/403 as Failure(isAuthError=true); when the heartbeat receives an auth error it calls prefs.clearCloudCredentials() (removing gatewayId, gatewayToken, isRegistered) and immediately calls registrationManager.register(), so a stale or lost token triggers automatic re-registration before the next heartbeat attempt.

HeartbeatManager.retryNow() resets the backoff ladder to 1s and sends a token into the conflated wake channel, canceling any in-flight backoff (or even the 60s interval) sleep; ConnectionSupervisor.retryNow() invokes it via the retryHeartbeat component callback when NetworkMonitor validates the network is online again, and the UI's manual Reconnect does too — without it a 5-second Wi-Fi re-association would wait out up to 5 minutes of the exponential ladder.

sendHeartbeat() first re-checks GatewayAccessPolicy.canTransmit(consent, isEnabled) and, if not registered or the token is blank, calls registrationManager.ensureRegistered() before POSTing; the start() loop also breaks to IDLE at the top of each iteration when consent is absent or the gateway is disabled, and the loop records lastHeartbeatAt on success.

HeartbeatManager exposes ConnectionState (IDLE, CONNECTING, CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, ERROR) via stateFlow, but the manager itself only assigns IDLE/CONNECTING/CONNECTED/DISCONNECTED — ERROR is set only by the UI layer (GatewayViewModel on a failed manual re-registration), and the GatewayViewModel derives its 'connected' chip from lastHeartbeatAt being within 90s plus isRegistered.

WebhookEngine.sendCloudEvent() is invoked from IncomingMessageDispatcher.dispatch() fire-and-forget for every incoming SMS; it requires isRegistered and a non-blank gatewayToken, derives a deterministic eventId as UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes of 'sender|date|first 100 chars of message' so reprocessing re-derives the same ID for backend deduplication, and posts {eventId, type: sms.received, sender, message, timestamp} to /api/gateways/events/sms with the Bearer token.

Cloud event uploads are guarded by a local idempotency cache in GatewayPreferences holding up to 500 sent event IDs (insertion-ordered FIFO trim, re-inserted at tail so retried events stay newest); a 2xx marks the event sent while a failure leaves it unmarked — and because SMS_DELIVER fires once, a permanently-down backend means the event is effectively lost with no app-side replay (backend-side retry handles downstream delivery).

WebhookEngine.sendIncomingSmsWebhook first enforces GatewayAccessPolicy.canTransmit(hasGatewayConsent, isEnabled) and skips ALL dispatch (local webhook and cloud event alike) when it fails; the local webhook additionally requires an HTTPS URL or it is rejected at dispatch.

The backend URL resolves through a three-level chain: the GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL Gradle property (via ./gradlew -PGATEWAY_BACKEND_URL=... or gradle.properties) is written into BuildConfig.GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL in app/build.gradle.kts; when absent the default is https://gaitway.autonomousone.in; and GatewayPreferences.backendUrl returns the stored cloud_backend_url value if present, otherwise the BuildConfig default.

Nothing is sent to the cloud backend unless versioned consent is present (storedVersion >= CURRENT_CONSENT_VERSION, currently 1) AND the supervisor-derived runtime isEnabled flag is true — canTransmit gates the heartbeat loop top and sendHeartbeat, the WebhookEngine dispatch entry, and registration blocks outright without consent; GatewayService refuses ACTION_START without consent.

revokeGatewayConsent() removes the consent version and accepted-at timestamp, resets isEnabled, gatewayDesiredEnabled, and autoStartOnBoot to false, and calls clearCloudCredentials() (drops gatewayId, gatewayToken, isRegistered); the view model also stops the service, so revocation stops registration, heartbeat, and forwarding and prevents credentials from resurrecting traffic after reboot.

gatewayToken and registrationSecret are stored in SharedPreferences under the enc:v1: prefix via SecureStore (AES/GCM with a hardware-backed Android Keystore key), legacy plaintext values are transparently re-encrypted on first read, and persistence is fail-closed since v2.6.10 — storeEncrypted throws when the Keystore is unavailable rather than demoting to plaintext, so callers see an empty value until the Keystore recovers or the secret is re-issued.

The Cloud Backend Gateway card and the other advanced transport cards in GatewayScreen are compiled but currently hidden behind showAdvancedGatewayModes = false, with the GMweb pull bridge positioned as the only recommended server connection; the effective cloud URL is still displayed by the REST endpoints card (cloud URL as base in 'Cloud Mode', display fallback https://gaitway.autonomousone.in) and the foreground notification text carries 'Cloud: <backendUrl>'.

The only JVM unit test covering the relay subsystem is GatewayAccessPolicyTest, which unit-tests the canStart (consent required) and canTransmit (consent AND enabled required) truth tables used at every cloud transmission boundary; BackendClient, HeartbeatManager, and RegistrationManager are Android-dependent and have no JVM tests, being exercised on-device via the gateway screen log flow, and scripts/test-gateway-api.ps1 targets the LAN API rather than the cloud backend.
